sb_prompt: WHAT ADVICE OR EXPERIENCE CAN YOU OFFER TO A PARENT ON HOW TO HELP A SON OR DAUGHTER CHOOSE A COLLEGE TO ATTEND?
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: How's it going?
ParticipantB: Pretty good, just wrapping up some paperwork at the front desk.
ParticipantA: Oh, nice. I'm currently managing a grocery store, so I'm pretty busy with inventory and staff stuff.
ParticipantB: Yeah, retail can be a grind, but it keeps you on your toes.
ParticipantA: Exactly, though I have to say, the whole "college choice" thing is really interesting to me. You know my cousin went through it last year?
ParticipantB: Oh yeah? How's that going?
ParticipantA: It's been a little rocky, honestly. He ended up picking a school way out of state just because his parents thought it looked "better" on paper, but he's miserable there.
ParticipantB: That sounds rough. I actually had a similar story with my own kid.
ParticipantA: Wait, really? You're a parent? I thought you were just working in an office.
ParticipantB: Yeah, I'm a receptionist, but my daughter is 19 now. She just started at a local community college instead of the big state university we wanted her to go to.
ParticipantA: That's smart actually. She says she's getting the same credits for half the price.
ParticipantB: Exactly! She was so stressed about the whole thing, like she was missing out, but she's actually doing better than I ever did in school.
ParticipantA: That's a good perspective. I was worried she'd make the same mistake as my cousin though.
ParticipantB: Well, we told her to just look at what makes her happy, not just the ranking.
ParticipantA: That's a real talk. My cousin's parents were so focused on the prestige, they didn't ask him what he liked studying.
ParticipantB: Yeah, parents can get so caught up in their own dreams for their kids sometimes.
ParticipantA: It's crazy. I'm actually telling my cousin's parents I think they should try him out at a smaller school for a semester if it's not working out.
ParticipantB: That's a solid plan. Sometimes stepping back a notch is the best way to find your feet.
ParticipantA: For sure. It's less pressure and more real-world testing.
ParticipantB: Definitely. It's about finding where they fit, not just where they *should* be.
ParticipantA: I like that. I guess I'll keep that in mind when I talk to him next week.
ParticipantB: Good luck with that. Feel free to call me if you need a sounding board.
ParticipantA: Will do. Thanks for the advice.
ParticipantB: Anytime.
ParticipantA: Okay, have a good one.
ParticipantB: You too.
